title: The Double Drop
premise: Xanthe Voss, a freelance interpreter who quietly settles disputes the peace process cannot touch, is approached by a man insisting she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of granting. He claims the debt belongs to her double, a woman using Xanthe's name and forged credentials to move through the same diplomatic circles, and he intends to collect from whichever of them is real. As the delegation collapses toward a staged 'accident' timed to the dawn extraction flight, Xanthe must infiltrate her impostor's network, untangle an inheritance that explains why someone needed to be her, and stop the attack before the plane becomes the alibi. In the end she lets her double take the fall for the conspiracy, walks onto the flight under a third identity, and chooses justice outside any courtroom — keeping the inheritance, and the impostor's debts, as her own.
about_author: Zephyrine Pemberton is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade in rooms where the real agreements were made in the pauses between sentences. She writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to be almost nobody.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Between sessions of a failing peace delegation, a stranger corners Xanthe in a hotel bar and thanks her for saving his life in Sarajevo — a trip she never took. He leaves a ledger page as 'interest owed.' The beat is unease: her careful invisibility has a crack in it, and someone else has been living inside her name.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. She verifies the ledger page against her own records and finds forged credentials — her name, her face, a parallel career. Tracing the forger leads to a dead broker's estate and an inheritance clause requiring a living 'Xanthe Voss.' The beat is cold dread: the impostor isn't hiding from her; she's the cover.

chapters.title: Two of a Kind
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. She engineers a meeting with her double, Mara, posing as a client. Mara is charming, cornered, and clearly working for someone above her. She hints the 'accident' is scheduled to coincide with the delegation's collapse. The beat is wary fascination — recognition of a self that chose differently.

chapters.title: The Delegation Dines
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. At the delegation's formal dinner, Xanthe interprets while reading the room for Mara's handlers. A seating 'mistake' places her beside the delegation's security chief, who mentions a maintenance inspection on the extraction aircraft. The beat is paranoia: every courtesy is a signal, every translation a possible misdirection.

chapters.title: Interest, Compounded
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. The stranger from the bar reappears, revealing he's the estate's executor and has been testing both women to see which deserves the inheritance. He offers Xanthe the truth of the will in exchange for letting the attack proceed — the delegation was never meant to succeed. The beat is temptation with a blade in it.

chapters.title: What the Interpreter Heard
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Reviewing her own session tapes, Xanthe finds a deliberately mistranslated clause that legally redefines the 'accident' as force majeure, shielding the plotters. She identifies the insider: the delegation's own chief of staff. The beat is grim clarity — the sabotage was written in language, her native territory.

chapters.title: The Long Night Before Dawn
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. With hours before the extraction flight, she and Mara form a brittle alliance: Mara wants out of her handlers' grip, Xanthe wants the attack stopped and the will honored. They trade identities for the night. The beat is reluctant trust between two versions of one woman.

chapters.title: Hangar Six
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Infiltrating the maintenance hangar, they find the sabotage is a fuel-line fault designed to read as fatigue failure. Mara's handlers catch them; the chief of staff arrives to tie off loose ends. The beat is terror and improvisation as Xanthe talks — in three languages — to keep them alive.

chapters.title: The Double Drop
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Climax: Xanthe uses the mistranslated clause against its authors, recording the chief of staff confirming the plot in the language his superiors believe she can't follow. Mara takes the blame on camera, trading her freedom for Xanthe's silence and the inheritance. The flight is grounded; the 'accident' never flies. The beat is triumph paid for in betrayal.

chapters.title: Boarding Pass, Third Name
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Resolution: the delegation limps home, the conspiracy buried as bureaucratic failure. Xanthe, now legally the inheritor, boards the rescheduled dawn flight under a new identity — Mara's real name. She keeps the ledger page as a reminder that debts, like identities, can be inherited. The beat is quiet, unburdened escape.
